PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 1.
FADE IN:
CAMERA FINDS the LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS. We move past a
raucous group of 9-YEAR-OLD BOYS playing kickball in the grass.
At this very moment, in the town of North
Thrush, Young Ned was...
PAN OVER TO
A tree. Underneath, YOUNG NED sits by himself, bouncing a
rubber ball.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...lonely.
Not terribly coordinated, he misses his own catch and the ball
sputters away from him, getting lost in the deep thicket of
grass, farther away from the playing children.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Unable to make friends at the Longborough
School for Boys, he often found himself
playing alone, with nothing but memories of
happier times to keep his company.
Ned slowly rises to retrieve his ball, but can’t find it. He
looks out at the beautiful meadow in the distance.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
What Young Ned did not realize was that beyond
the meadow and under that same orange sky,
someone he loved was remembering him.
OMIT
HARD CUT TO:

scenes.heading: EXT. YOUNG NED’S OLD HOUSE - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: DIGBY! Sitting on the porch, looking glum. A FOR SALE sign in
the foreground.
His dog, Digby. In fact, 3 days prior, Digby
had made a decision.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
Digby looks left. Then right. When he’s certain no one is
there to catch him, he races off the porch into the yard.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Wearied by his own loneliness back in Coeur
d’Coeurs and sensing his master’s sorrow,
Digby set out on a mission.
A paw-ful of dirt FLIES into CAMERA, which transitions us into:
OMIT
Digby bounds along until his attention is drawn over to:
Uncertain as to his exact destination, he
ventured into the great unknown, guided only
by the compass of his heart.
STOCK FOOTAGE - BUILDING ON FIRE
ON DIGBY
He cocks his head, noticing.
THE RED FIRE BOX on the street corner. With his paw, he PULLS
DOWN THE LEVER.
OMIT

scenes.heading: EXT. DIFFERENT PART OF URBAN STREET - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Digby continues on his incredible journey as a FIRE ENGINE
SCREAMS by. Digby continues his trot.
Despite numerous distractions, Digby was
determined to find Young Ned, the boy who had
given him a second chance at life.
OMIT
Young Ned is where we left him, staring out toward the meadow.
And who was his best friend.
He is about to give up on the ball, when he sees something
moving in the distance. A dog... running... Could it be?
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
It is! Young Ned GASPS in recognition of his furry friend.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Upon doing so, Digby proved that love can
overcome any obstacle.
TIME SLOWS as Man and his Best Friend hurtle toward one another
in a Chariots of Fire-inspired sprint and then... STOP.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The reunion was bittersweet, however, as they
instantly remembered the restrictions of their
friendship.
Digby drops the ball at Young Ned’s feet.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
They could not touch. Or Digby would die.
Young Ned smiles. Digby happily pants.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Still. It was enough.
Young Ned grabs a branch off the tree above him and uses it to
scratch Digby in his happy place.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
That day, Digby vowed he would never again
allow himself to be separated from his master.
Young Ned picks up the ball and throws it. Digby leaps high
into the air...
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - FRONT DOOR - MORNING

lines.text: ...and catches it.
NED (O.S.)
Good boy.
REVEAL NED, having just walked into the Pie Hole with Digby. He
lovingly regards CHUCK, working away in the kitchen.
The Pie-maker did not wish to be separated
from Chuck...
ON Chuck, in the kitchen, squeezing homeopathic antidepressant
drops onto a pie.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Who, in turn, did not wish to be separated
from her aunts Lily and Vivian, who continued
to be challenged by social phobias.
Chuck happily slides the pie into the oven.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Unbeknownst to the Pie-Maker, Chuck secretly
baked homeopathic mood enhancers into pies for
her aunts, hoping that a slice a day would
herbally lift their spirits.
Ned appears behind her, just as she’s removing her apron:
You’re up early.
Chuck quickly hides the homeopathic antidepressant dropper. She
whirls around, like a woman who has just been caught doing
something wrong. She smiles, quickly covering.
Couldn’t sleep.
Lumpy mattress?
Lumpy dreams. Which are a lot more vivid now
than they were before I died. Isn’t that
interesting? One of those little things.
Chuck notices a few small welts on Ned’s face. Stings,
specifically. He tries to hide them.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
What are those?
I, uh, got bit.
Those are beestings. How’d you get stung by
so many bees? And what happened to the bees
that stung you? That’s a suicide attack.
Not in this case. They, uh, sort of stung me.
Died. And then flew away again. Then some
other bees died.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED: (2)
I wonder if their honey will taste different
because they died? Wouldn’t that be
interesting? One of those little things?
Ned smiles, digging her.
I wanna show you something.
He motions for her to follow him, and she can’t help but smile.

scenes.heading: EXT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - ROOFTOP - DAY

lines.text: In the center stands a fully-functioning apiary. The BUZZING of
bees swarming within. Chuck stands before it, unable to believe
her eyes. Ned is warm with happy. He did good.
Bees!
Your bees.
My bees? You mean--?
Not those bees. New bees. For you.
Technically still your bees, just not the bees
you knew. But I’m sure they’re equally nice.
You do realize beekeeping within city limits
is completely illegal.
Yes. And I’m almost sure I don’t care.
I can not-care enough for both of us.
Ned smiles and Chuck can barely contain herself.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
We can plant wildflowers on rooftops and be
unorthodox urban honey pioneers.
(overwhelmed)
Thank you! Thank you! Thank you! I wish I
could hug you right now. I know that I can’t,
but just know that I want to.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED:
I do.
As CAMERA PULLS OFF of Chuck and Ned...
As Chuck considered her future as an
unorthodox urban honey pioneer...
OMIT
Where we see a frustrated OLIVE struggling to open the front
door. Digby watches her from inside, amused.
Olive Snook considered how the man she loved
seemed to be in love with someone else.
She finally busts through and trips, falling nose to nose with
Digby.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Her affection for the Pie-Maker had not
wavered, despite the romantic threat of a dead
girl who wasn’t dead.
You’re a big help.
Digby licks her nose. She rises, dusting herself off just as
Chuck and Ned ENTER from the back door.
On the contrary, Olive’s resolve had only
increased since the realization that Chuck
indeed was supposed to be dead.
(cheery)
Good morning.
(equally cheery)
Good morning.
Olive fakes a smile to Chuck before heading toward the back.
Ignorant of the Pie-Maker’s gift, Olive
assumed Chuck had faked her own death. She
would keep the secret for now...
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
Ned is about to pre-heat the stove, when he realizes:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
As Chuck kept her secret from the Pie-Maker.
There’s a pie in my oven.
Oop! That’s mine.
(before he can ask)
I was practicing.
I smell cheese. Is it quiche?
She takes it from him with a smile. He melts.
I baked Monastery Gouda into the crust. Tart
apple filling. I thought I would try it.
Chuck gingerly places the box on top of the rest of the delivery
pile as Olive approaches from the main dining room.
The first mood-enhancing pie Chuck secretly
baked for her aunts was pear with Gruyère.
You know what would be delicious? Pear with
Gruyère crust. Bet that would be real good.
Yes, it would.
Unbeknownst to Chuck, Olive understood the
deliciousness of pear and Gruyère...
Chuck stares at Olive, who only returns a sweet smile. Chuck
pushes the pie box toward the DELIVERY BOY, who is now waiting.
(to the delivery boy)
Thank you.
The delivery boy glances at the Coeur d’Coeurs pie box and puts
it back on the counter.
...because she secretly delivered that first
mood-enhancing pie to Aunts Lily and Vivian.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED: (2)
Olive breezes past and SCOOPS UP the box.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
As she would deliver this one. But not before...
THWUD! All heads turn toward the window.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...a collision occurred.
A crack in the glass of the Pie Hole window has been created,
courtesy of the pigeon below it. A pigeon missing one wing.
Olive gingerly lifts her up, while Ned looks at his window.
I think she’s dead. Can you feel a heartbeat?
Olive tries to deposit the bird in Ned’s hands. He moves away.
I don’t... do heartbeats.
They feel like this.
Olive takes Ned’s hand and presses it to her heart. We hear the
THUMP-THUMP-THUMP of her heart. Time stops for a moment...
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Thump-thump. Thump-thump.
...until EMERSON and Chuck appear directly behind Olive:
(re: the pigeon)
Is that a dead bird? Why you touching a dead
bird? Throw that away. It’s swimming with
disease. And you serve food.
Oh, don’t be such a drama queen. I can wash
my hands. And she doesn’t look diseased.
It’s dead. And it’s a bird. It’s diseased.
Olive pulls the pigeon away from Emerson, defensively, which
causes her to BRUSH the bird against Ned. Which causes you-know-
what. The bird SQUAWKS and comes back to life.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED:
It’s a miracle bird! It’s swimming with
miracles, not disease.
Maybe you should let me hold it.
Aw, do you have to? Clearly, she’s been
through a lot. And she seems happy to be here.
He shoots her an “Are you kidding?” glance.
Having brought a dead thing back to life, the
Pie-Maker fretted over which pint-sized animal
would pay for that life with its own.
As Ned starts his watch, wondering what’s going to drop dead
around him, the women hover over the helpless bird.
I wonder how she lost her wing.
She doesn’t seem to be in any pain.
She’s not. Probably. Probably not in pain.
But what do I know? I’m not a bird.
Pigeon.
Or a pigeon. I was pigeon-toed as a child,
but a pair of orthopedic shoes solved that.
Ned spots a SQUIRREL nearby and sensing his imminent demise:
NED (CONT’D)
Shoo.
(to the pigeon)
Don’t worry. I know just what to do with you.
(to Chuck)
I recently made the acquaintance of a pair of
bird lovers. I’ll consult them.
Olive was referring to Aunts Lily and Vivian.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED: (2)
Really? I used to know a pair of bird lovers.
Chuck also referred to Aunts Lily and Vivian.
“Used to”? Did they die?
A death was involved.
How unfortunate.
They were both so busy referring and
inferring, they failed to notice that 60
seconds had passed.
While Ned’s focus is on shooing away the squirrel...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The Pie-Maker could not afford such a luxury.
A DEAD BIRD falls from the sky, going PLOP on the sidewalk.
There’s an awkward pause, then Ned shrugs:
It’s raining dead birds.
Olive walks out into the street to get a better look at the sky:
What is going on up there?
VVVVVHHHHHHHRRRRRROOOOM! All four heads turn to see a CROP
DUSTER PLANE fly into a small building, CRASHING THROUGH THE
SIDE. There’s no explosion, no fire. Just a CRASH!
What was going on up there was this:
OMIT
The front of the plane sits squarely inside the living room of a
one-bedroom apartment. BRADAN CADEN’S DEAD BODY lies prostrate
along the fuselage, having been catapulted through the front
glass.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED:
An out-of-control crop duster crashed
headfirst into the Broadview Luxury Apartment
Complex, killing the pilot instantly.
A handsome man in his 30s, CONRAD FITCH offers testimony to
POLICEMEN among the remains of his newly-destroyed home. EMT
WORKERS are already on the scene. Bradan’s DEAD BODY is ZIPPED
into a body bag.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
His body was catapulted out of the cockpit and
into the living room of one Conrad Fitch.
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON Ned, Emerson and Chuck in the doorway.
Does this qualify as ambulance chasing? I’m
asking without any judgement at all.
If you’re asking without any judgement, then
yes. It does. Look for body bags.
That’s not our thing.
Your thing is waking up dead people. My thing
is finding dead people for you to wake up.
The dead body is placed on a gurney and wheeled toward them.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Found one.
Why can’t we just be here as concerned
citizens of the world?
Because Big Daddy needs some new yarn.
Just because there’s a dead body doesn’t mean
you’re gonna get paid.
Just because there’s vodka in my freezer don’t
mean I have to drink it. Wait. Yes, it does.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 12.
CONTINUED: (2)
He’s not wrong. Plane crash into a building
could mean a civil suit. Criminal suit.
Negligence. Pain and suffering. Negligent
pain and suffering...
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON Emerson and Ned, surprised and not by
Chuck’s knowledge of the law.
Chuck fostered her love of the law by
volunteering as a stay-at-home juror for a
paraplegic judge.

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: CAMERA PUSHES IN ON YOUNGER CHUCK, phone pressed to her ear.
(to phone)
We the jury, in the case of the Commonwealth
versus Duralde, find the defendant guilty.
We HEAR the gavel CLACK over the phone. Chuck smiles.
RESUME - INT. BUSTED APARTMENT
Emerson, Chuck and Ned, as before. Chuck steps aside as the EMT
wheels the body out of the room. She STUMBLES BACK over a piece
of debris, causing her to fall backward in SLOW MOTION.
Unable to catch Chuck when she fell, the Pie-
Maker was forced to step aside...
CONTINUE SLOW MOTION as Ned is poised to catch her, but instead
of extending his arms, he takes one giant step backward allowing
Chuck to fall. Chuck and Ned exchange a SLOW MOTION GLANCE.
TIME RETURNS TO NORMAL as a muscular arm scoops Chuck ‘round her
waist and catches her. She looks up to see who her knight in
shining armor is. It’s not Ned.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...allowing another man to catch her.
CHUCK’s POV: An upside-down Conrad. He’s cute and frazzled.
Thanks...
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 13.
CONTINUED:
(shell-shocked)
Forgive the mess. Maid comes tomorrow. I
should cancel that.
Do you live here?
Until very recently.
Can you put her down, please?
Conrad does as instructed.
Your collection of nautical plates survived.
Just then, the shelves holding the collection of NAUTICAL PLATES
collapses, sending the plates SHATTERING to the floor.
They were Franklin Mint.
I’m sorry.
It’s okay. I’m okay. I’ll be okay. I was
feeling like I should simplify my life anyway.
Chuck’s heart goes out to him. Which irks Ned.
Chuck’s heart went out to the man with a plane
in his living room, despite the Pie-Maker
wanting her heart for himself. Suddenly,
ambulance chasing didn’t seem like a bad idea.
(clears his throat)
The ambulance is leaving.
Chuck walks over to Ned, leaving Conrad to hyperventilate alone.
You go ahead. I’m gonna stay and see if
there’s anything I can do.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 14.
CONTINUED: (2)
I’m sure he’s fine. Statistically speaking,
his day can only improve. Dead pilot on the
other hand probably has lots of last wishes.
Like maybe he wished he turned left.
You don’t need me for that.
She does have a point.
But--
Will you stop arguing with the woman? We got
a dead man to talk to.
The facts were these:
SLOW PUSH IN
ON A MANILA FILE FOLDER. A hand opens it up and we see:
A BLACK-AND-WHITE PHOTOGRAPH of a clean-cut, flannel-wearing man
in his 50s, Bradan Caden. He stands beside his FARM WIFE in
front of his plane.
One Bradan Caden, an agricultural aviator, was
53 years, 21 weeks, 5 days, 6 hours and 19
minutes old when his crop duster collided with
the Broadview Luxury Apartment Complex.
FLIP the photograph to the left-hand side of the file, and we
come upon the first page of a fairly thick insurance policy.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It was 17 minutes after the collision and Mr.
Caden’s Aviator’s Aviation Insurance agent had
already rejected the claim on his life policy
before the claim was even made.
A large rubber “SUICIDE” stamp hits the page and the file is
closed.
ON Emerson and a newly-jealous Ned walking inside.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 15.
CONTINUED:
Did you see the way he just swept in?
Yeah? So?
I don’t sweep. Sweeping isn’t my style.
It is a little showy.
It’s a lot showy. What’s a roof full of bees
compared to someone who can catch her when she
falls? I can’t catch her, Emerson.
Can’t suck on her toes, neither.
(off Ned’s look)
Some women like that.
When they get to the front desk, they find our CORONER sitting
across from BECKY CADEN, the pilot’s widow. She speaks slowly
and deliberately, stunned by events.
Bradan Caden’s wife, Becky, believed her husband
was not suicidal and was, in fact, a happy man.
He was a happy man.
(off the coroner’s blank stare)
These insurance people, making assumptions
about a person’s disposition.
One should never assume.
An insurance agent can’t speak to the
deceased’s state of mind.
They turn to see Emerson and Ned standing in the doorway.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
They didn’t know the deceased. You did.
Pardon me. I couldn’t help overhearing your
conversation and I believe I can be helpful.
Emerson catches the coroner staring at him suspiciously.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 16.
CONTINUED: (2)
May I have a word with you?
OMIT
Emerson closes the door behind the coroner as they both step
into the hall to have a private conversation.
Why you bothering this poor woman? You and
that white boy got some kind of shifty going
on. I don’t know what. But you’re shifty.
I’m here as a concerned citizen of the world.
You making a dime, concerned citizen?
Maybe one or two to rub together.
Well, then. Flies land on me, they pay rent.
Ned stands awkwardly, surreptitiously checks to make sure
Emerson is occupying the coroner. Becky stares. Finally:
Excuse me. I’m just gonna...
Ned quickly ducks into:
Ned UNZIPS the body bag on the gurney REVEALING Bradan Caden’s
corpse. SHARDS OF GLASS stick out of his face. (NOTE: These
are bloodless wounds and will be played as darkly humorous.)
Ned sets his watch, touches him. He FLASHES.
INCLUDE BRADAN CADEN’S POV - NED
As seen through a KALEIDOSCOPE with multiple reflections of Ned
on the various pieces of glass.
Hello.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 17.
CONTINUED:
You that fellow that jumped on my plane?
No. A... fellow jumped on your plane?
I was hijacked.
He waves his hand in front of the shards of glass, digging it.
Is that why you crashed? Mister Caden?
Oh, yessirree. I was dusting soybeans, or
getting ready to, when dippy in a prison
orange jumpsuit climbed aboard.
Dippy was on the plane when you crashed? But
you’re the only dead dippy-- body they found.
Then dippy’s not dead. Lucky him.
The door swings open behind Ned and he quickly touches Bradan
Caden one last time and he FLASHES dead. Ned turns to see
Emerson, Becky and the coroner squeezed into the doorway.
What in the hell?
The plane was hijacked.
How’d you come by that?
DNA-ish.
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
FADE IN:
Olive stands outside the door. In one hand, she carries a
gilded cage housing the one-winged pigeon. In the other, a pie
box. On her face, a smile. She rings the bell.
Olive Snook came to Coeur d’Coeurs on a wing
and a prayer. With a gilded cage housing the
mono-winged bird in one hand and a pie box in
the other, she set out to expose Charlotte
Charles -- aka, Chuck -- as a faker of deaths.

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS' HOUSE - DINING ROOM - DAY

lines.text: CLOSE ON: A GIANT EYE looking through a magnifying glass.
LILY (O.S.)
It’s a carrier pigeon.
PULL OUT to reveal LILY inspecting the pigeon through the glass,
pulling a tube off the pigeon’s leg.
Diseases or messages?
Lily turns and reveals the tube from the pigeon’s leg.
Both.
A bird with gossip. That’s exciting.
VIVIAN reaches for the tube, but Lily snatches it back.
Do you open other people’s mail?
Who’s the people and how hard is it to open?
Vivian laughs, which surprises all three of them.
I don’t know where that came from.
What’s gotten into you?
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED:
What’s gotten into you?
What had gotten into both of them was their
niece’s homeopathic pie.
Embarrassed, Lily and Vivian turn to Olive. They compose.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
As with any mood-stabilizer, moods were a bit
inconsistent at the start.
Olive turns their attention back to the mono-winged pigeon.
Do you think you can fix her?
She’ll only go out there and get hurt again.
Coyotes will have their way with her.
Lily puts the pigeon back in its cage and joins Vivian at the
table, cutting herself a slice of pie.
But she was meant to fly. She needs to
fulfill her destiny and deliver that message!
A bird that stalks down his narrow cage can
seldom see through his bars of rage!
Olive dramatically pulls open the curtains. LIGHT pours in. As
does a lot of dust. She COUGHS.
It wouldn’t hurt to try.
That’s the spirit! And once we fix Pidge, we can
celebrate by taking a trip to the Pie Hole. It’s
a nifty spot with lots of interesting folks. You
never know who you might run into.
Lily and Vivian freeze, pie just inches from their mouths.
With that, Olive Snook set her plan in motion.
Why would we go out for pie when you just
brought us one?
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED: (2)
I’ll think of a reason.
While Olive Snook considered how to get Lily
and Vivian out of their rut...
The door swings open REVEALING Emerson and Ned standing on the
other side of the police tape. They both duck under. The
apartment is empty. Chuck and Conrad are nowhere to be found.
The Pie-Maker was considering worst-case
scenarios, not only for a rogue hijacker who
he had been hired to find by Becky Caden, but
for Chuck and the man who caught her in a way
the Pie-Maker never could...
They’re not here. This is bad.
Maybe they took a stroll.
That would not make it better.
What’s worse? The two of them locked up in
the trunk of a hijacker’s car, or sipping
mimosas in a hotel room?
I’m not a fan of either scenario and what’s
that smell?
I thought it might be your cologne.
Who wears cologne?
(defensive)
I wear cologne.
Ned notices the steamer trunk operating as a coffee table. Two
empty cups of coffee sit on top. One smudged with lipstick.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED:
(sadly)
Look. They had coffee.
As Ned leans down to pick up the cup, he smells the bad smell
again. Even stronger this time.
NED (CONT’D)
Whoa. There’s something bad in there.
He opens the trunk. AN OLD DEAD GUY wearing a specialty bowling
shirt is stuffed inside. Emerson reacts.
NED (CONT’D)
Is he the hijacker?
What kind of fool hijacker goes and hides
himself inside a damn coffee table?
Emerson grabs Ned’s hand and touches the Old Dead Guy with it.
SPARK! Our dead guy (who should feel vaguely like Milton Berle)
comes to life. He struggles to move, but he’s crammed in tight.
Damn gout. I’m so cramped up, I feel like I’m
stuffed in a trunk.
You are stuffed in a trunk.
Don’t contradict an old man. It’s
disrespectful.
Did you hijack that plane?
What plane? Oh. Hell is fire. That thing
flew right into my apartment.
This is your apartment?
What I just say?
(then, back to his story)
There I was, enjoying my daily prunes and
psyllium powder and hoping for the best, when
suddenly I see a plane heading right for me--
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 22.
CONTINUED: (2)
If this is your apartment, then who’s Conrad?
What is this, the idiot brigade?
Which is when they notice the name stitched onto his bowling
shirt. It reads:
Conrad.
Oh.
Ned quickly re-deads the old guy. OFF Ned, fearing the worst...
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON Chuck and Conrad as they ENTER.
Do you like pie?
Be criminal not to like pie.
TIME CUT TO:
OMIT
Conrad and Chuck both have a slice of pie and glass of milk.
Everything I am. Everything I was.
Everything that represented me as a human
being was in there. I have to start over.
Chuck studies him a moment.
I lost everything once. And you know what--
Did a plane fly into your living room?
No.
Was it arson?
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 23.
CONTINUED:
No. It was something else. But I felt this
queer thrill of... opportunity.
To get new stuff?
To let go of everything about me I didn’t like
and hold onto everything about me I did.
I just met you but I can’t imagine anything
about you that isn’t something to like.
He reaches out and touches her hand. Chuck eyes it.
Chuck’s first thought was to quickly pull her
hand away. Her second thought was how nice it
felt to have someone hold her hand.
He pulls his hand away.
I’m sorry. Was that your boyfriend... the guy
who took a step back to let you fall?
Oh, he didn’t let me fall. It was actually a
very affectionate gesture. In context.
If it was only the Pie-Maker’s hand...
Can I ask you a small favor? I’d like to hold
your hand. Just for a moment. But you can’t
say anything, and I’m gonna close my eyes.
He stares at her a moment, then:
All right.
Conrad pauses for a moment before laying his left hand on the
table. Chuck puts her hand in his and...
CHUCK’S POV - CONRAD
He’s sitting across from her. Her eyelids close and when they
re-open, we’re looking at Ned. It’s his hand she’s holding.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 24.
CONTINUED:
FANTASY PIE HOLE BOOTH
Chuck and Ned sit opposite each other holding hands.
In that moment, Chuck was holding the Pie-
Maker’s hand... if only by proxy.
ON CHUCK, SMILING, EYES CLOSED
CHUCK’S POV - DARKNESS (EYES CLOSED)
Her eyes open and she’s looking at Conrad. CAMERA ADJUSTS TO
REVEAL Ned outside the window, momentarily stunned by the hand-
holding.
It was the proxy that concerned the Pie-Maker.
Conrad’s smile quickly turns as he sees Emerson and Ned entering
the restaurant. He jumps up.
I’ve got to pee.
He races toward the bathroom just as Ned and Emerson ENTER.
How’d it go?
Where’d he go?
Conrad? To the bathroom--
As Emerson heads toward the bathroom:
He’s not Conrad, he’s the hijacker.
(then, noticing)
And he’s not in the bathroom.
As Ned races to the kitchen:
Boy, you miss one trip to the morgue...
Conrad is almost out the back door, when Ned slides under the
table and grabs onto his arm.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 25.
CONTINUED:
Conrad yanks himself away from Ned, causing the door to smash
into Ned’s face and Conrad’s arm to POP off.
Ned stumbles backward, holding onto the arm minus the body.
He’s too stunned to go any further. Emerson races out the back
door, in an attempt to catch up with Conrad. We stay with Ned
and Chuck, both staring at the prosthetic arm. Then:
Is this the hand you were holding?
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 26.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - DAY

lines.text: TIGHT ON the prosthetic arm which reads PROPERTY OF HARBOR BAY
CORRECTIONAL FACILITY. Ned and Chuck sit in a booth. In the
background, we see Emerson talking on the phone in the kitchen.
He’s a great, big fibber then, isn’t he?
A great, big fibber whose hand you were
holding. What’s that about?
I was... if you have to know, I was pretending
I was holding your hand.
Is that supposed to make me feel better?
Well, yeah.
On one hand, it does make me feel better.
Then on the other hand -- the hand you were
holding -- it doesn’t.
He’s an escaped convict.
You didn’t know that when you held his hand.
And P.S. -- not only is he an escaped convict,
he’s a hijacker who prevented thousands of
crops from being aerially fertilized. And he
stuffed a surly old dead guy in a trunk.
I’m not saying he isn’t guilty. And I’m not
saying I am. I’m saying it wasn’t about him.
No, it’s about Becky Caden, wife of Bradan
Caden, the woman your handyman widowed when he
chose to crop dust someone’s living room.
Emerson crosses toward Ned and Chuck.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 27.
CONTINUED:
Did you catch him?
One-armed bitch was speedy. But I checked in
with my people at the prison--
You have people? That’s so neat.
Did you find out anything good?
Yes. And we’re gonna need shovels.
Eyebrows of intrigue go UP, as we...
We see a slightly younger and geekier version of “Conrad” in a
dull brown suit. He looks nervous and guilty as he checks the
place out, making sure no one else is around.
Emerson Cod had learned three things. First:
The man they knew as Conrad Fitch was actually
one Lemuel Weinger, a low-level employee of a
company called OrNeN Energy.
Once he’s sure he’s alone, he removes a heavy file from inside
his suit jacket, pulls out an industrial-sized shredder from
underneath the desk and starts SHREDDING DOCUMENTS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Second: OrNeN was an energy based corporation
known for several types of trading. Plastics,
steel and insider. The latter cost Lemuel his
right hand.
The frantic shredding goes awry when Lemuel’s right arm gets
(comically) worked through the machine.
No-No-No-No-Noooooo!!!!!!!!
Hearing the cry, a JANITOR opens the door and turns on the
light. Lemuel is instantly CAUGHT.
It also cost him his freedom.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 28.
TIGHT ON Lemuel as prison bars close. He turns to discover a
craggly OLD MAN eating bad food off a cafeteria tray, wearing a
wifebeater and a pair of tighty whities. This does not bode
well.
Third: During his incarceration, Lemuel became
known as Lefty Lem. A name given to him by
his cellmate, Jackson Lucas, an infamous
diamond thief whose final escapade resulted in
a buried treasure that was never recovered.
Lemuel extends his fake arm toward Jackson, who stabs it with
his fork before shaking it.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Even after he died.
Jackson magically DISAPPEARS, leaving Lemuel alone in the cell.
TIGHT ON THREE SHOVELS hitting a mound of dirt. PAN UP to
REVEAL our Mod Squad in a prison cemetery. The headstone
reveals they’re digging into the grave of Jackson Lucas.
Luckily, death was not an obstacle for the Pie-
Maker, which is how he suddenly found himself
in a prison graveyard, digging up the body of
one Jackson Lucas.
So Fake Conrad was a white-collar criminal.
That makes much more sense...
Ned grunts. Chuck notices his mood.
Gonna get paid once by the pilot’s widow after
we prove her husband’s death wasn’t a suicide.
(to Ned, pointedly)
Dead bodies always lead to paydays.
Yeah, yeah, vodka in the freezer.
Gonna get paid twice when the Feds give us the
reward for kicking Lefty’s ass back to the
clink where he belongs.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 29.
CONTINUED:
Looking forward to that...
Gonna get paid thrice by finding Jackson’s
buried booty.
THUNK! Ned’s shovel hits something. Emerson smiles.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Come to Papa.

scenes.heading: EXT. POTTER’S FIELD - A LITTLE WHILE LATER

lines.text: The earth has been removed to REVEAL a ROTTING COFFIN. The
three of them stand around it. No one is eager to touch it.
You might want to avert your eyes. There’s a
good chance he’ll be on the dewy side.
Damn. I hate dewy.
Emerson closes his eyes and keeps them that way. Chuck does
not. Ned takes a deep breath, but before he opens it:
Are you mad at me?
Ned looks at her, casually:
Why would I be mad?
For holding someone’s hand that wasn’t yours.
Seriously? In a prison graveyard? That’s
where you’re having this conversation?
Ned faces the coffin again. Deep breath, and he OPENS it!
I would’ve preferred a little more eyeball.
Just touch the damn thing.
Wait.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 30.
CONTINUED:
For what?
A little dignity.
She takes a pair of sunglasses out of her purse and puts them on
the corpse. Ned can’t help but smile.
Thanks.
Ned touches him. ANGLE ON a decent-looking CORPSE now wearing
Chuck’s sunglasses. He sits up.
I can’t see anything. Am I blind?
The good news is you’re not blind. Bad news
is you’re dead.
Makes blind seem like a walk in the park,
doesn’t it?
(eyes still closed)
Where’d you bury your loot, Jack?
Why should I tell you?
Good karma. It’s like currency in the
afterlife.
Jackson considers.
Inside the old windmill on the VonRoenn farm,
at the bottom of the stairs. How much that
worth?
Plenty. Ask him ‘bout Lefty.
Did you tell him where you buried it?
‘Course I did. Owed him that much.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 31.
CONTINUED: (2)
What did you owe him for?
For keeping the fire alive...
Ned quickly re-deads him.
We got a windmill to find.
As Emerson leads them out of the graveyard:
Chuck’s fire may not be alive as far as her
aunts Lily and Vivian were concerned...

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS' HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY

lines.text: A white hot lamp stands over the dining room table where Lily
and Vivian work diligently on something we don’t yet see. Olive
stands a few feet away, a tray of implements beside her.
But Olive was doing her best to reignite it.
Brackets.
Olive looks at the tray and passes her tiny metal brackets.
Ribbon.
Olive passes the ribbon.
Be-jeweler.
Olive lingers on a small plastic bead gun.
Can I do one?
Maybe the last one.
Lily takes the plastic bead gun. And starts punching beads.
If you’d like we could be-jewel Pidge’s
birdhouse when we’re done.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 32.
CONTINUED:
Pidge’s house is only temporary. No sense be-
jeweling an empty home. Is there, Pidge?
Something so sad about an empty birdhouse.
When one of our birds dies, we taxidermy it
immediately. Put it right back on its perch.
Vivian does wonders with sand and thread.
And little marble eyes. It’s like our birds
never left us at all.
You can’t put everything back on its perch.
Olive knows exactly to what she’s referring.
Must have been all kinds of horrible for you
when Charlotte left.
She didn’t leave. She died.
And no amount of sand and thread and little
marble eyes will ever bring her back.
But Olive didn’t need sand or thread or little
marble eyes to bring Chuck back. She needed a
confluence of events.
Wing!
And she was about to get one.
Olive looks up at the taxidermy bird above her head and quickly
SNAPS off one of the wings and hands it to Lily.
Can I do the last be-jewel?
I already did it.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 33.
CONTINUED: (2)
Lily steps away from the table, finally allowing us to see the
TINY BIRD HARNESS. A bizarre contraption made of fabric,
ribbon, be-jewels and one movable wing. Olive is impressed.
What do you think, Pidge?
Pidge raises its new, colored wing and examines it, then glances
back toward Olive, Lily and Vivian.
And while Olive, the aunts and Pidge looked
forward to the next step in their journey...
An antique sign tells us we’re in the--
PAPEN COUNTY HISTORICAL SOCIETY.
Tons of windmill models, large and small, fill the room. REVEAL
A DEAD CURATOR, eyes rolled into the back of her head, sitting
at her desk, surrounded by miniature windmills.
...another journey had reached a dead end.
But Lefty Lem’s was only just beginning.
REVERSE to find Ned, Chuck and Emerson staring at the dead body.
Is she dead?
Lefty Lem has officially taken the lead.
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 34.
FADE IN:
Our Mod Squad is looking at the dead curator.
You think Fake Conrad killed her?
Ockham’s razor. All things being equal, the
simplest solution tends to be the best one.
I used to believe that. Until you brought me
back from the dead. Kinda screws the theory.
Ned sets his watch, touches the woman. No spark. Hmmm...
Maybe your finger needs a new battery.
Emerson grabs Ned’s hand.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Let me try.
Emerson pokes her harder with Ned’s hand, causing her head to
flop over and hit the desk, which wakes her up with a SNORT.
Ow.
EMERSON / NED
(point at each other)
He did it.
Must’ve dozed off again. Can I help you?
We’re looking for a windmill. A VonRoenn
variety of windmill.
That’s funny. Another young man was just here
asking about the VonRoenn mill.
Did the man happen to have one arm?
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 35.
CONTINUED:
As a matter of fact he did.
(sneeze/cough)
Ockham.
Bless you.
Thank you.
The windmill. What happened to it? Razed?
Wrecked? Rebuilt? Removed?
Retired. No farm. No use. Got shipped off
to NARM some twenty years ago.
Why would they send it to ‘Nam? Do the
Vietnamese need windmills?
(noticing the pamphlet)
NARM. National Area of Retired Mills.
The VonRoenn mill has been preserved as an
historical landmark. Got a map right here--
At which point she immediately slips back into a deep sleep.
Now that’s narcoleptic. Necrophiliac is the
other one.
Yes.
As our Mod Squad looks at the map, PUSHING IN on the image of
the VonRoenn windmill, whose blades are distinctively RED...
Armed with a new plan, the Pie-Maker and
associates left the narcoleptic curator to her
dreams. Meanwhile, back in Coeur d’Coeurs, a
tiny friend was planning her own escape.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 36.

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS' HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY

lines.text: CLOSE ON our now fully-harnessed pigeon. She studies herself in
the hand mirror they’ve set up on the dining room table. REVEAL
Olive studying Vivian, who is studying Pidge’s empty cage.
Olive’s disdain for Chuck was split in two.
One for stealing the Pie-Maker’s heart, and
the other for breaking the aunts’.
Olive sits next to Vivian. She produces Pidge’s message tube.
You know you wanna.
Lily would be so displeased. There was an
incident. I read something I shouldn’t have.
And then life went horribly awry. Lily never
forgave me. Said she did. But she didn’t.
Olive sets the message tube down.
Well, now I’m more interested in that story.
(eyes the empty birdhouse)
Let’s put Pidge back in her house.
Pidge has left the building. I’m sorry and
I’m sorry her empty birdhouse makes you sad.
Maybe you should fill it with all your
Charlotte sadness and hang it in a special
place in your soul.
That’s an awfully sad birdhouse to have
hanging in one’s soul.
Lily ENTERS, carrying a martini.
Hang it someplace you don’t have to see it.
It won’t always be sad. It’ll be the happiest
little birdhouse when you’re ready.
(singsong, not singing)
Make a little birdhouse in your soul.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 37.
CONTINUED:
It’s so catchy, Vivian can’t help but join in, also singsongy:
Not to put too fine a point on it.
Say she’s the only bee in your bonnet.
Make a little birdhouse in my soul.
Don’t encourage her.
She sits on the other side of Olive and watches the pigeon
awkwardly finish making her way across the table.
LILY (CONT’D)
I think she looks divine.
No sooner have the words escaped her lips when... FLAP-FLAP-
FLAP... the pigeon TAKES FLIGHT straight out the window!
LILY (CONT’D)
Son of a bitch.
WAIT! You forgot your message! COME BACK!
Olive rushes out to chase Pidge. Lily and Vivian move toward
the doorway...
As the aunts watched Olive scream for help,
they considered their own birdcage and wondered
if they were ready to leave it behind.
...but do not dare inch beyond the frame.
OMIT
HUNDREDS OF MILLS of various shapes and sizes for miles and
miles. HYPER ZOOM IN through the melee to the VonRoenn windmill
we saw on the map. Same distinctive red blades.
A few miles away...
Continue ZOOMING IN to the KITCHEN where ELSITA (20s), a pretty
woman full of country goodness, is looking into the distance...
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 38.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Looking out across the fields and hills, a
beautiful woman named Elsita waited for the man
she loved to make her heart complete. Little
did she know, Lefty Lem was already on his way.
There is a KNOCK at the door. Elsita opens the peephole and
talks through it with a bit of a drawl--
What the hell do you want?
REVEAL--
I’m from the Papen County Historical Society.
We would like to photograph the premises for
the 87th annual “Mills of the Wind” Papen
County collector’s calendar.
Where’s your camera?
(long, awkward pause)
In the car.
You’re lying. But I’m bored.
LEFTY
Scowls. Didn’t think it was that transparent. We move behind
him as he scratches his back with the AX he’s hiding, and we...
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 39.
FADE IN:
CAMERA finds our harnessed pigeon flying about 10 feet off the
ground, and looking pretty good. CAMERA SLOWS, letting the bird
go as we hear the approaching CAR before we see it.
OLIVE / VIVIAN
(singing)
I’M YOUR ONLY FRIEND, I’M NOT YOUR ONLY FRIEND,
BUT I’M A LITTLE GLOWING FRIEND, BUT REALLY I’M
NOT ACTUALLY YOUR FRIEND, BUT I AM --
THE “WOODY” station wagon tears by in pursuit if the bird.
Lily drives, begrudgingly. Digby sits beside her in the
passenger seat. Olive and Vivian are in the back.
BLUE CANARY IN THE OUTLET BY THE LIGHT SWITCH.
WHO WATCHES OVER YOU? MAKE A LITTLE BIRDHOUSE
IN YOUR SOUL --
NOT TO PUT TOO FINE A POINT ON IT. SAY I’M
THE ONLY BEE IN YOUR BONNET --
OLIVE / VIVIAN
MAKE A LITTLE BIRDHOUSE IN YOUR SOUL.
Never mind the singing. Keep your eye on that
bird!
The car tears into the distance. Off Olive and Vivian’s
giggles...
OMIT
Suburbia whirs past them. Ned and Chuck sit in the front seat,
the partition between them. Emerson is in the back, wishing he
had his own partition.
You know what our problem is.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 40.
CONTINUED:
If you’re referring to the touching thing, I
see it as more of an obstacle than a problem.
Pretty big obstacle.
Not compared to our other problems.
We have other problems?
I’m gonna kill myself...
There’s so much I’m learning about you.
Such as?
You’re a romantic.
When the mood strikes.
You’re jealous when the mood strikes.
Everyone’s a little jealous. I mean, if
you’re not a little jealous, you’re probably--
(off her)
Can we not talk about this?
The answer to your query is yes.
No. Actually, I wanna talk about this. I
could let it go, but like the cat, it will
come back. Which I wouldn’t call annoying,
but there’s not really a great way to say half-
annoying, which it is, a little bit.
He may have gone too far... Then she smiles--
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 41.
CONTINUED: (2)
See? Isn’t this neat? Here we were thinking
all we had was one big problem, when in fact
we have hundreds of little problems that we’re
gonna have to work out before we even GET to
the big problem. Which means we’re like
everyone else in the world.
Except I still can’t catch you.
Emerson leans forward.
We’re taking two cars next time.
Chuck leans back in her seat, a little more worried than she was
before...
Lefty is on one knee, tying Elsita to a wooden chair with one
hand and his mouth, still holding the ax.
That’s a big ax.
I promise I’m not gonna hurt you. This is
just a precautionary measure.
(off his struggle)
Wouldn’t it be easier if you put the ax down
and then tied the rope?
He looks at her. She is completely at ease. He sighs and sets
the ax down, continues tying...
ELSITA (CONT’D)
Funny you really are a “one-armed bandit.”
Your name’s not “McClappin,” is it? As in,
“The sound of one hand...”? Names are
destiny. You think Duane Cloggin ain’t gonna
grow up to be a plumber, think again.
(notices)
Didn’t really use bows to tie me up, did you?
You take a hostage like you tie your sneakers.
What is your problem?
Lefty starts to knock on each stair, looking for a hollow spot.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 42.
CONTINUED:
I was born into a life of wind millery. You
gonna listen, or are you gonna keep knocking?
I’m listening. “You were born into a life of
wind millery...”
Always waiting on the wind to show up so you
can work. No good at waitin’. Tired of it.
You sure it’s just the wind you’re awaitin’ on?
Her look tells us he might be onto something, then:
Did you just say “awaitin’”? ‘Cause if you’re
mimicking me, I will be outta these girly bows
faster than a snake through weeds.
He pauses, genuine, maybe noticing how pretty she is...
I wasn’t thinking and I apologize. I have a
lot on my mind and I’m in a bit of a rush.
Where you rushin’ to?
Don’t really know yet.
Well, you should probably figure that out.
They both pause in the attraction...
ELSITA (CONT’D)
Go back to your knocking.
As he swings the ax into the bottom stair of the staircase--
CLOSE ON the aunts’ car with Olive hanging out the window.
C’mon, Pidge! You can do it!
(to the aunts)
Not even a breeze to help poor Pidge. Which
is kind of ironic, given the surroundings.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 43.
CONTINUED:
PULL OUT to REVEAL the aunts are driving through NARM! And the
pigeon is heading straight for our windmill...
The pigeon, growing fatigued with each flap of her
taxidermy wing, knew something the others did not:
THWUD! Our pigeon crashes directly into our windmill, slides
down onto the balcony.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Her journey was almost complete.
Olive and the aunts SCREECH to a halt. They cringe.
Oooph.
Lefty nervously moves to the window.
What was that?
It’s my bird!
Elsita unties herself and rushes to her, picks her up.
ANGLE - PIGEON
Looks up, still alive.
It’s my bird.
What’re you on about? It’s my bird.
I’ll prove it. I wrote the note.
(looks)
Where’s the note?
He looks for the tube, which isn’t there. Olive calls out:
Hello? Can I have my bird back?
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 44.
CONTINUED:
LEFTY LEM / ELSITA
Your bird?!
Yes, “my bird.” She has a message and she has
to... carry it. It’s what she does.
Olive holds up the message tube, as the aunts appear behind...
That’s my message.
Elsita reaches for the message as well, their hands touching.
Elsa?
I’m Elsita. Jackson?
I’m Lem.
Elsa was my mamma.
Jackson was my prison bunkmate.
As Elsita and Lem stare into each other’s eyes--
Is “bunkmate” a euphemism for...
Not in this case, ma’am.
A much younger Jackson, dressed like Indiana Jones and carrying
a satchel across his back, battles the wind.
He looks hunted as he makes his way toward the lone windmill
standing at the center of the empty farmland.
There was a bitter chill in the air the night
Jackson Lucas found refuge in the VonRoenn
windmill. Already five days on the lam, he
knew the police were closing in.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 45.
Jackson takes out a satchel filled with diamonds and stuffs it
inside the already-broken staircase.
To preserve his dreams of one day owning an
art gallery in Mexico, Jackson decided to bury
his stolen treasure in the staircase of the
seemingly-abandoned property.
Jackson hears a CREAK from above. He quickly looks up to find a
beautiful YOUNG WOMAN wearing nothing but a white nightgown and
a flimsy shawl to keep her warm. A BABY PIGEON sits on her
shoulder.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
His heart stopped, however, when he saw an
angelic creature descending the stairs. Her
name was Elsa. And this was her windmill.
Their eyes meet. Hers are kind and unafraid.
My name is Elsa. This is my windmill.
It was love at first sight. Knowing he had
very little time left...
He nervously looks over his shoulder, and then:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...he kissed her. It was a perfect moment.
SUDDENLY the door BUSTS OPEN and two POLICE OFFICERS appear,
breaking up the kiss.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The next moment was not.
As the police quickly cuff him and drag him toward the door,
Elsa and Jackson keep their eyes locked on one another. She
calls out, tearfully:
I’ll write you!
The door closes and Elsa is left alone. She looks at the baby
pigeon on her shoulder and is struck with an idea.
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 46.
Elsa, still wrapped in the same shawl, writes by candlelight.
Elsa kept true to her word. For the next 20
years, she and Jackson continued their love
affair by correspondence...
When she finishes the note, she puts it in a tube that attaches
to the pigeon’s leg.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...letters sent to and fro with the help of
her virtually-untraceable carrier pigeon.
TIGHT ON an older, sickly Jackson as he reads the note that was
written for him. He melts with love. Pidge waits nearby for
her next mission.
Until the day Jackson knew he would no longer
be able to keep his promise.
Jackson looks over to the other end of his cell. REVEAL Lefty
Lemuel, watching from his cot.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Someone else would have to do it for him.
PUSH IN on Lefty as he begins to understand his new purpose.
TIGHT ON the same image of Lefty, now sitting in the same spot
Jackson had sat in twenty years earlier.
After Jackson died, I started to plan my
escape. It took two years, and all that time
I kept writing to Elsa.
PULL OUT TO REVEAL that across from him is Elsita, Olive and the
aunts. Pidge sits on a stand. Olive is enthralled by the story
she just heard. Lily is dubious.
LEFTY LEM (CONT’D)
At first I was writing out of loyalty to the
man who taught me the ropes in prison. But
after a while, I started to develop...
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 47.
CONTINUED:
A condition?
For Elsa. At least, I thought it was Elsa.
Mamma made me swear on her deathbed that I’d
keep writing to Jackson. Said it’d break his
heart to learn she’d died. But each letter he
wrote was more beautiful than the last, and I
found myself looking forward to them.
Your letters were beautiful, too.
They gaze into each other’s eyes, history repeating itself.
What’s the big whoop?
Pidge has brought them together.
How did she lose her wing?
I took her on the plane with me when I busted
out of prison. Flew out the window after we
took off. Went right through the propeller.
Pidge crashed the plane! Oh, Pidge.
Where are the diamonds?
VIVIAN / LILY / OLIVE
Diamonds?
Elsita lifts her long skirt, revealing a WOODEN LEG. She opens
a compartment inside her leg, revealing sparkling diamonds.
Holy crap.
Holy crap.
Suddenly, a violent KNOCK. Lefty JUMPS to his feet, grabbing
his ax:
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 48.
CONTINUED: (2)
Now, now. Let’s not panic. I’m sure it’s
just the mailman, or maybe a windmill-to-
windmill salesman. Lemme handle it.
Olive calmly rises and heads toward the...
Olive approaches the front door and looks through the peephole.
She pulls her head back in disbelief--
(to herself)
Hell’s bells...
She looks again--
OLIVE’S FISH-EYE VIEW: A three-shot of Ned, Emerson and Chuck.
SLOW PUSH IN on CHUCK...
As Olive peeped through the peephole, it
occurred to her that while the carrier pigeon
was safe inside the windmill, the same could
not be said for the sitting duck currently
waiting on the doorstep.
Olive’s hand moves to open the door. It looks like Chuck’s
secret is about to be revealed!
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 49.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: INT. WINDMILL - FRONT DOOR - DAY - CONTINUOUS

lines.text: Olive’s hand stays on the doorknob, debating.
This was the moment Olive Snook had been
waiting for. She need only open the door to
expose Chuck’s deceit to the aunts, and the
Pie-Maker could be hers.
As she ponders these happy eventualities, Olive incrementally
opens the door...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It was everything Olive wanted...
Resolutely, Olive widens the door quickly, but SUDDENLY STOPS
SHORT of swinging it wide enough for the aunts to see through...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and yet...
Olive turns and looks at Aunts Lily and Vivian, who chat happily
with the young couple.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...she knew that the aunts would be
traumatized by the discovery that the late
Charlotte Charles was late no more. In that
moment, Olive felt the angry fire in her heart
extinguished by a light breeze...
OMIT
BACK TO SCENE
Olive’s gaze softens at the sight of her new friends.
She had grown fond of Lily and Vivian, and
could not bring herself to hurt them.
Olive steps out alone, closes the door behind her. Our
threesome is shocked, but Olive puts on a happy grin.
Afternoon, gang!
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 50.
CONTINUED:
Olive?
What the hell are you doing here?
Pie delivery.
(significantly, to Chuck)
Tart apple, I believe.
With those two words, Chuck knew.
Chuck turns her head slightly and notices--
THE BROWN WOODY
Parked in front of the windmill.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Her aunts were inside.
Olive...
If you know what’s good for you, and I think
you do, you’ll give me two minutes.
Why?
What for?
Okay.
Goody then.
Olive RE-ENTERS the house, shutting the door behind her. Ned
and Emerson look at Chuck, who smiles and shrugs.
The lovers can’t stop staring at each other. Olive starts
collecting her things. She’s ready to go.
(eyes on Elsita)
Who was it?
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 51.
CONTINUED:
Wrong mill. Must happen all the time around
here, huh? Anyway. I feel awful we’ve taken
up so much of your day. We should be going.
She gathers the aunts and steers them toward the back door.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Do you mind if we use your back door? I
wanted to take a peek at your garden on the
way out...
As they head out the back door...
Emerson checks his watch. Chuck and Ned stare at the door, not
looking at one another over the following:
Ned?
Hm?
Remember before when I told you all the things
I liked about you?
Jealous. Romantic. Jealous.
(then)
I felt I had to say it twice.
Right. Well, now might be a good time for you
to make a list of all the things you like
about me.
Why?
‘Cause that way, if stuff happens... just
remember the list.
Time’s up.
Emerson removes his gun from his cosy, and prepares to kick in
the door.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 52.
Lily drives as Olive sits next to her. Vivian sits by the
passenger window.
There. Now wasn’t that a nice outing?
I could use a drink.
Young people depress Lily because she’s afraid
of dying.
LILY
Bumps along in silence...
As Lily wondered whether she was afraid of
dying or simply missed feeling alive, she
allowed herself one deep breath of fresh
country air.
Lily takes a deep breath, glancing in the rearview mirror...
I don’t think we’ve been out once since--
ANGLE - REARVIEW MIRROR
Chuck stands by the windmill.
LILY (CONT’D)
--Charlotte?
An arm of the windmill rotates in front of the place where Chuck
stands, and when it lifts away -- she’s gone...
CAR
No need to yell her name. I think Heaven’s
closer than we think.
I agree.
Lily stares again in the mirror, shaking it off. Off Olive,
knowing she made the right decision...
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 53.
Emerson, Ned and Chuck barge through the door, breaking up Lefty
and Elsita’s steamy embrace. Emerson points his gun:
Hand up!
Lefty raises his hand in one-armed, un-armed surrender.
CAMERA CLOSES IN ON his one good arm extended in the air.
CLOSE ON the same hand being handcuffed.
CAMERA PULLS OUT ON a POLICE OFFICER as he CUFFS Lefty and pulls
his arm behind his back. Then, realizing there’s no second arm
to cuff it to, he lets it dangle. He pushes Lefty into the cop
car while Emerson stands beside him, counting his reward money.
ANGLE ON the front door of the windmill. Where Elsita watches
the action from afar, her heart breaking. As the cop car starts
to drive away, Elsita sprints toward it.
Lemuel! I’ll write you!
Lefty pumps his one good arm out of the car window.
The Pie-Maker and the girl he called Chuck
marvelled at love’s power to conquer all
obstacles. Distance and time...
OMIT
The aunts sit on their couch, staring ahead as they eat their
pie, looking wistfully at the portrait of Chuck.
...hardship and pain...
OMIT
From across the room, Olive wistfully watches Ned --
...a lack of reciprocation...
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 54.
CONTINUED:
-- who is wistfully watching:
CHUCK. Who is sitting in a booth with Becky, a pie box sits on
the table between them.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...even death...
Your husband was a great pilot. He didn’t
kill himself -- a pigeon did, by accident.
Becky smiles, relieved. Chuck hands her a check and the pie.
OMIT
Lefty sits in his cell, writing “Elsita” on a note. Pidge
stands next to him.
With Pidge’s help, the long-distance love
affair of Lefty and Elsita continued to soar.
THE CAMERA FOLLOWS the bird’s ascent, PANNING ACROSS THE SKY TO:

scenes.heading: EXT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - ROOFTOP - DUSK

lines.text: Chuck, in full beekeeper uniform, looks out over the horizon.
She seems content, but not yet happy.
And the Pie-Maker realized that while some
obstacles may never disappear...
A tap on Chuck’s shoulder. She turns, sees--
Ned, in full BEEKEEPER WEAR (including GLOVES and NETTED HAT).
He stands by an OLD-FASHIONED RECORD PLAYER with RCA-STYLE
amplifying cone.
Care to dance?
He drops the needle. A SONG STARTS TO PLAY. Probably a TANGO.
(smiles big)
Yes, please.
And they do. Suit to suit.
PUSHING DAISIES #103 "Pigeon" 10/05/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 55.
CONTINUED:
You can always find a way to work around them.
Dip!
Ned dips her low, CATCHING her with ease. Chuck smiles.
You caught me.
He smiles and pulls her up into a twirl. The two would-be
lovers dance slowly as the sun sets behind them.
